items.title: platform_disabled skills config ignored by Signal gateway

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

`skills.platform_disabled.signal` in `config.yaml` is ignored by the Signal gateway. Despite configuring 107 skills to be disabled for the Signal platform, all 129 skills still appear in the system prompt's skill index, and all 26 tools are still passed to the model.

## Impact

With 129 skills (16K chars) + 26 tools (33K chars schema), the system prompt + tools payload reaches ~53K chars. Local LLMs (tested: gemma4:26b, hermes3, qwen3:14b, mistral-small3.1) consistently fail to call tools when the combined payload exceeds ~25K chars. They respond with text instead of making tool calls.

This makes Hermes Agent effectively unusable with local models when many skills are installed.

## Reproduction

1. Set `skills.platform_disabled.signal` in config.yaml with a list of skill names
2. Set `platform_toolsets.signal` to a reduced toolset list
3. Restart gateway (`hermes gateway run --replace`)
4. Send a message via Signal
5. Check the session JSON — skills index and tools count are unchanged

## Verification

```python
# Config is parsed correctly:
from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_platform_tools
signal_tools = _get_platform_tools(config, 'signal')
# Returns: ['clarify', 'cronjob', 'memory', 'session_search', 'skills', 'terminal', 'todo']
# Count: 7 ✓

# But actual session has 26 tools and 129 skills in the index
```

`platform_toolsets.signal` also appears to be ignored — the session shows the full `hermes-signal` toolset (26 tools) instead of the configured 7 toolsets.

## Config (relevant sections)

```yaml
skills:
  creation_nudge_interval: 15
  external_dirs:
    - ~/prj/ai-server/hermes-skills
    - ~/.agents/skills
  platform_disabled:
    signal:
    - apple-notes
    - apple-reminders
    # ... 107 skills total

platform_toolsets:
  signal:
  - terminal
  - skills
  - memory
  - session_search
  - clarify
  - todo
  - cronjob
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.10.0 (2026.4.16, commit 816e3e37)
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 (Mac Mini M4 Pro 24GB)
- Ollama v0.21.0
- Signal gateway via signal-cli SSE
- Model: hermes3:latest (also tested gemma4:26b, qwen3:14b)

## Debug Report

- Report: https://paste.rs/58ztT
- agent.log: https://paste.rs/PPEuY
- gateway.log: https://paste.rs/hsYB8

(auto-deletes in 6 hours)

## Suggested Fix

`build_skills_system_prompt()` in `agent/prompt_builder.py` reads `get_disabled_skill_names()` but may not be receiving the platform context when called from the gateway. The `_platform_hint` variable (line 611) relies on `HERMES_PLATFORM` env var or session context, which may not be set correctly for Signal gateway sessions.

items.title: [Feature]: Support ntfy as a native Messaging Provider

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Currently, Hermes Agent supports several messaging platforms for user interaction and notifications. However, for users running Hermes in self-hosted environments (NAS, private VPS) or air-gapped setups, existing integrations (like Discord or Slack) require external cloud dependencies and complex bot registrations.

### Proposed Solution

Integrate ntfy (an HTTP-based pub-sub notification service) directly into the send_message core logic or as a dedicated Messaging Provider.
Key benefits:
• Privacy-focused: Supports self-hosted instances (e.g., ntfy.example.com).
• Minimalist: No heavy SDKs; uses simple HTTP POST requests.
• Authentication: Support for Bearer Tokens for private topics.
• Rich Notifications: Native support for priority levels (high, urgent), tags (emojis), and action buttons/clickable URLs.

### Alternatives Considered

Implementation as a Skill: I initially developed this as a Python-based Skill. While functional, it creates a "circular dependency" logic flaw: a Skill is an action the agent must decide to call during a task. However, notifications for long-running autonomous tasks (like a daily GitHub summary) or system alerts need to be part of the output transport layer. If the agent’s execution environment encounters an issue, it cannot "call a skill" to report it; it needs a native messaging provider to reach the user.

### Feature Type

New tool

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

### Debug Report (optional)

```shell

```

items.title: [Bug]: resolve_session_name sanitizes gateway_session_key without length truncation, overflows Honcho's 100-char session ID limit
items.body:
### Bug Description

Matrix adapter session keys passed through HonchoClientConfig.resolve_session_name() (plugins/memory/honcho/client.py) are sanitized but not length-bounded, producing session IDs that overflow Honcho's Pydantic max_length=100 on Session.id. Bug introduced in v2026.4.16 with the new gateway_session_key code path; v2026.4.13 predates this path and does not exhibit the problem (at the cost of losing per-chat memory isolation for Matrix rooms).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure hermes v2026.4.16 to use Honcho as memory provider: set  `memory.provider: honcho` in config.yaml and place a valid honcho.json  in $HERMES_HOME pointing at a reachable Honcho v3.0.6 instance.
2. Connect the Matrix adapter to any homeserver whose sanitized hostname  exceeds ~13 characters (common patterns: IP-encoded DNS like sslip.io / nip.io, Tailscale .ts.net, subdomains of public registrars).
3. Send any message from the room to the bot.

### Expected Behavior

Honcho initializes successfully; Matrix session appears in the Honcho workspace (peers / sessions / messages populated, per-chat memory works).

### Actual Behavior

`plugins.memory.honcho: Honcho init failed` on every Matrix-origin message:

```
{'type': 'string_too_long',
 'loc': ['body', 'id'],
 'msg': 'String should have at most 100 characters',
 'ctx': {'max_length': 100}}
```

Workspace ends up with 0 peers / 0 sessions — memory is effectively disabled for Matrix chats.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)


### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

v0.10.0 (2026.4.16)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`plugins/memory/honcho/client.py :: HonchoClientConfig.resolve_session_name` returns the incoming `gateway_session_key` after sanitizing but without any length bound:

 ```python
if gateway_session_key:
    sanitized = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]+', '-', gateway_session_key).strip('-')
    if sanitized:
        return sanitized
```

For Matrix, the adapter builds the key as `agent:main:matrix:group:!<room>:<homeserver>:<event-id>`. After sanitization:

```
len = 26 + R + HS + EV
      ^    ^   ^    ^ event ID hash length (Matrix spec, room v4+: 43 chars)
      |    |   homeserver hostname length (dots → hyphens, length unchanged)
      |    room localpart length (Synapse/Dendrite/Conduit: 18 chars)
      "agent-main-matrix-group" (23) + 3 separators
```

Two of the three variables are effectively frozen by Matrix protocol / reference implementation:

- **EV ≈ 43**: Matrix spec (room version ≥ 4, mandatory since 2019) defines event ID as `$` + `base64url_unpadded(sha256(canonical_json(event)))` → always 44 chars including `$`, 43 after sanitize. Cryptographic, cannot be shortened without losing uniqueness / tamper-evidence.
- **R ≈ 18**: Synapse (and Dendrite, Conduit) generate an 18-char random opaque room identifier via `random_string(18)`. No homeserver-level setting exposes this.

That leaves the homeserver hostname as the only variable. Honcho Session.id has Pydantic max_length=100, so solving `26 + 18 + HS + 43 ≤ 100` gives: 

```
HS ≤ 13 chars
```

13 chars is a tight budget — short single-label domains (e.g. `m.co`) still fit, but many common patterns (IP-encoded DNS like sslip / nip, Tailscale `.ts.net`, subdomains of public registrars) exceed it, so a sizeable share of real deployments hits this.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run hermes
2. Send any prompt.

### Expected Behavior

Empty prompt line upon agent's response

### Actual Behavior

Character strings like 20;1R21;1R23;1R24;1R25;1RR1;1R appears in the prompt line and the CLI may freeze after the agent's final answer

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

```shell
Report and agent log saved as an attachment on bug description
```

### Operating System

Debian 13.4 (Trixie)

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

v0.10.0 (2026.4.16)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
╭─ ⚕ Hermes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
    Now let me implement the fix. The Application constructor accepts an output parameter — I'll create a Vt100_Output with enable_cpr=False and pass it:

╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  ┊ 🔧 preparing patch…
  ┊ 🔧 patch     /home/debian/.hermes/hermes-agent/cli.py  1.1s
  ┊ review diff
a//home/debian/.hermes/hermes-agent/cli.py → b//home/debian/.hermes/hermes-agent/cli.py
@@ -10364,7 +10364,19 @@
             'voice-status-recording': 'bg:#1a1a2e #FF4444 bold',
         }
         style = PTStyle.from_dict(self._build_tui_style_dict())
-
+
+        # Disable CPR (Cursor Position Report) queries — prompt_toolkit sends
+        # \x1b[6n (Device Status Report) to detect cursor position, and the
+        # terminal replies with \x1b[row;colR. Over SSH/cloudflared tunnels
+        # these responses leak as raw text like "20;1R21;1R" and flood the
+        # display. Disabling CPR forces prompt_toolkit to use heuristic
+        # fallback instead, eliminating the leak with no visible side effects.
+        try:
+            from prompt_toolkit.output.vt100 import Vt100_Output
+            _cpr_disabled_output = Vt100_Output.from_pty(sys.stdout, enable_cpr=False)
+        except Exception:
+            _cpr_disabled_output = None
+
         # Create the application
         app = Application(
             layout=layout,
@@ -10372,6 +10384,7 @@
             style=style,
             full_screen=False,
             mouse_support=False,
+            **({"output": _cpr_disabled_output} if _cpr_disabled_output else {}),
             **({'cursor': _STEADY_CURSOR} if _STEADY_CURSOR is not None else {}),
         )
         self._app = app  # Store reference for clarify_callback

The change is at line 10368 in cli.py. Next time you run the CLI interactively (via hermes), the 20;1R garbage should stop appearing.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Did a self-review through the AI agent:

Root cause: prompt_toolkit sends \x1b[6n (Device Status Report) escape sequences to the terminal to query the current cursor position. The terminal replies with \x1b[row;colR. When you are connected over an SSH + cloudflared tunnel, these CPR responses sometimes leak as raw text into the terminal display, producing the 20;1R21;1R23;1R... strings you see. This also causes the perceived lags because the terminal is processing escape sequences instead of content.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

The fix: Before constructing the prompt_toolkit.Application, we now create a Vt100_Output with enable_cpr=False and pass it to the Application. This tells prompt_toolkit to skip sending cursor position queries entirely — it uses a heuristic fallback instead. The UI behavior is identical; the only difference is no \x1b[6n queries get sent, so no CPR responses can leak.

items.title: Gateway API server rejects image payloads >1MB due to missing client_max_size on aiohttp Application

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Report: Gateway API server rejects image payloads >1MB due to hardcoded body size limits

### Summary

The hermes gateway API server (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`) has two separate hardcoded 1MB body size limits that prevent sending images or other large payloads via the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. This makes vision/multimodal usage impossible with images larger than ~750KB (which base64-encode to >1MB).

### Environment

- Hermes version: latest
- Deployment: Docker
- Trigger: Sending an image attachment via any OpenAI-compatible client to the hermes gateway

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure hermes gateway as an OpenAI-compatible backend in any client
2. Send a chat completion request containing an image >1MB (base64-encoded in the request body)
3. Observe `413 Request body too large` response

If you patch `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`, you then hit a second error:

4. Observe `400 Invalid JSON in request body`

This is because aiohttp's `web.Application` has its own default `client_max_size` of 1MB, which silently truncates the body before it reaches the JSON parser.

### Root Cause

Two separate limits in `api_server.py`:

**Issue 1** — hardcoded middleware limit that rejects based on `Content-Length` header:
```python
MAX_REQUEST_BYTES = 1_000_000  # 1 MB default limit for POST bodies
```

**Issue 2** — aiohttp `web.Application` created without `client_max_size`, so it defaults to 1MB and silently truncates large bodies before they reach the JSON parser:
```python
self._app = web.Application(middlewares=mws)
```

### Suggested Fix

Make the limit configurable via environment variable, and apply it consistently to both the middleware and the aiohttp application:

```python
MAX_REQUEST_BYTES = int(os.environ.get("HERMES_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES", 20 * 1024 * 1024))  # 20MB default
```

```python
self._app = web.Application(middlewares=mws, client_max_size=MAX_REQUEST_BYTES)
```

This ensures both limits are consistent, configurable, and large enough to support realistic image payloads in multimodal workflows.

items.title: [#5] Phase 3 — End-to-End VLM Benchmark on Real Floor Plans
items.body:
## Objective
Design and implement the Phase 3 end-to-end VLM benchmark that measures Gemma4's full visual reasoning capability on real SCDF floor plans, measuring both perception and reasoning jointly.

## Background
Phase 1 (text-only) and Phase 2 (pipeline components) feed into this sprint: once each component works independently, we run the full integrated benchmark against Gemma4 31b as the VLM.

## Deliverables
- [ ] `benchmarks/run_vlm_benchmark.py` — CLI tool:
  - Accept floor plan image + Fire Code clause subset
  - Run full pipeline (perception → structured text → Gemma4 reasoning → verdict)
  - Compute end-to-end accuracy, per-dimension scores, timing breakdown
  - Output: `benchmarks/results/phase3_vlm/{run_id}/result.json`
- [ ] Dataset: compile benchmark dataset from:
  - 4 real audit cases (Findings_audit_plans_28Nov25.txt) with known verdicts
  - 50+ synthetic clause-condition pairs from Fire Code JSON
  - Each entry: (floor_plan_image OR structured_detections, clause_text, question, expected_verdict)
- [ ] Run full benchmark on Gemma4 31b (Ollama) — report results
- [ ] Error analysis: per-case failures, top error modes, clause types with lowest recall
- [ ] `benchmarks/results/phase3_vlm/report.md` — human-readable summary with all metrics

## Evaluation Metrics
- **End-to-end accuracy**: % of cases where Gemma4 verdict matches expected verdict
- **Clause recall**: % of relevant clauses correctly identified as applicable
- **Reasoning quality**: 0-5 score per case (per rubric from Sprint 3)
- **Perception quality** (if using Falcon Perception): detection precision/recall on symbol localization
- **Timing**: total pipeline latency, per-stage breakdown

## Success Criteria
- Full benchmark runs end-to-end with all metrics computed
- Error analysis identifies top 3 failure modes
- Report published to `benchmarks/results/phase3_vlm/report.md`

items.title: [Bug]: Auxiliary auto fallback fails on OpenRouter 403 credit/key-limit errors and may not skip the concrete failed backend

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body: ### Bug Description When auxiliary tasks run with `provider=auto`, and face 403 responses due to OpenRouter key/spend limits, auxiliary requests may **raise immediately** instead of **triggering provider fallback** to the next backend.” A related issue is that the fallback can skip the wrong backend (or skip nothing useful), causing ineffective retries, as there does not seem to be a concrete label passed by the caller ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure auxiliary resolution as `auto` (default). 2. Set an OpenRouter key/account in a depleted/key-limited state so requests return `403` with text like `Key limit exceeded`, `spending limit`, or `total limit`. 3. Ensure another provider is available (for example Codex OAuth, Nous, or custom endpoint) so fallback is possible. 5. Trigger an auxiliary call (for example compression/session search/web extract). 6. Observe request handling in `call_llm`/`async_call_llm`. ### Expected Behavior 1. `403` spend/key-limit responses should be treated as fallback-eligible payment exhaustion (same class as `402` for this purpose). 2. Auxiliary fallback should skip the actual failed backend and continue to the next available provider in the chain. 3. Auxiliary task should succeed on a downstream provider when one is available. ### Actual Behavior 1. `403` OpenRouter key-limit/spend-limit errors do not seem to be classified as payment exhaustion, and thus not triggering fallback. 2. In fallback-triggered paths, failed-backend identity may be too coarse if concrete backend metadata is not propagated, which can lead to poor skip behavior. 3. Auxiliary calls can fail even when another provider is configured and healthy. Screenshot below shows 3 tries with the same model and same error instead of trying a fallback provider: ### Affected Component Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell Debug report uploaded: Report https://paste.rs/JyerH agent.log https://paste.rs/z2GhQ ``` ### Operating System MacOS 26.4 ### Python Version _No response_ ### Hermes Version _No response_ ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) 1. Payment-error classification was too narrow and focused on `402`/generic patterns, missing common OpenRouter `403` key-limit wording. 2. `_try_payment_fallback()` itself only skips what it is told (`failed_provider` string); it does not discover backend identity on its own. 3. Call sites previously could pass a non-concrete provider value (for example coarse auto/provider context) instead of the concrete resolved backend label, so skip logic could be imprecise. 4. Because auxiliary fallback is chain-based, incorrect failed-backend identity undermines the main purpose of “advance past the backend that just failed.” ### Proposed Fix (optional) 1. Extend `_is_payment_error()` to treat OpenRouter `403` key/spend-limit responses as payment exhaustion signals. 2. Persist concrete resolved backend metadata on clients and thread it through cache/call paths. 3. Use that resolved provider label in `call_llm` and `async_call_llm` when invoking `_try_payment_fallback()`. 4. Keep fallback scoped to `auto` mode and to backend-unavailable classes (payment exhaustion + connection errors), so we do not hide request-shape or model/config bugs. 5. Add regression tests for: - OpenRouter `403` key-limit path triggers fallback - fallback receives concrete failed backend label - async path mirrors sync behavior ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: max_tokens/max_completion_tokens selection only checks URL host, breaks custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints serving gpt-4o/4.1/5.x/o-series

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

When a **third-party OpenAI-compatible endpoint** (a self-hosted gateway, an OpenAI proxy, or OpenRouter) serves one of OpenAI's newer model families — `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-5*`, `o1`, `o3`, `o4` — the agent silently sends `max_tokens`, and the server rejects the request with HTTP 400:

```json
{"error":{"code":"unsupported_parameter","message":"Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.","param":"max_tokens","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Every turn hard-fails. The URL-based detection at [`run_agent.py:2456-2465`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/run_agent.py#L2456) (`_max_tokens_param`) only treats `api.openai.com` as direct-OpenAI, so any custom base URL fronting a gpt-5 / gpt-4o / o-series model is misclassified as "old / uses max_tokens".

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Point hermes at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint that is **not** `api.openai.com` but **is** serving a new-family model:
   ```bash
   export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://my-openai-gateway.example.com/v1
   export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
   export OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.4          # or gpt-4o-mini, o3-mini, etc.
   ```
2. `hermes chat` and send any message.
3. The first chat completion call returns HTTP 400 `unsupported_parameter`.

### Expected Behavior

`_max_tokens_param` / `auxiliary_max_tokens_param` / `_build_call_kwargs` emit `max_completion_tokens` whenever the target model belongs to a family known to require it, **regardless of the base URL** — because the constraint is model-enforced at the server, not URL-enforced at the client.

### Actual Behavior

All three call sites only check `base_url_hostname(...) == "api.openai.com"` and send `max_tokens` on every other host. Custom gateways 400 immediately.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop — chat completions parameter selection).

### Root Cause

Three sibling sites share the same URL-only logic:

1. [`run_agent.py:2456-2465`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/run_agent.py#L2456) — `AIAgent._max_tokens_param`
   ```python
   def _max_tokens_param(self, value: int) -> dict:
       if self._is_direct_openai_url():
           return {"max_completion_tokens": value}
       return {"max_tokens": value}
   ```
2. [`agent/auxiliary_client.py:2089-2104`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/agent/auxiliary_client.py#L2089) — `auxiliary_max_tokens_param`
3. [`agent/auxiliary_client.py:2608-2618`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/agent/auxiliary_client.py#L2608) — inline branch in `_build_call_kwargs`

Ironically the same file already carries a *model-name* helper [`_model_requires_responses_api`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/run_agent.py#L2424) that recognises `gpt-5` by prefix — but that logic only drives API mode selection, not kwarg selection.

### Proposed Fix

Add a shared helper in `utils.py`:

```python
def model_forces_max_completion_tokens(model: str) -> bool:
    """Return True for model families that require ``max_completion_tokens``."""
    m = (model or "").strip().lower()
    if not m:
        return False
    if "/" in m:
        m = m.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    return (
        m.startswith("gpt-4o")
        or m.startswith("gpt-4.1")
        or m.startswith("gpt-5")
        or m.startswith("o1")
        or m.startswith("o3")
        or m.startswith("o4")
    )
```

And OR it in at all three sites:

```python
# run_agent.py
if self._is_direct_openai_url() or model_forces_max_completion_tokens(self.model):
    return {"max_completion_tokens": value}
```

Vendor prefixes (`openai/gpt-5.4`) are handled by stripping at `/`, so OpenRouter-style names also match.

### Tests

Existing `TestMaxTokensParam` in `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py` only flexes the URL axis — it doesn't set `agent.model` and never exercises the name-based fallback, which is why this slipped through. The fix should add:

- Custom endpoint + `gpt-5.4` → expects `max_completion_tokens`
- OpenRouter + `openai/gpt-4o-mini` → expects `max_completion_tokens`
- Custom endpoint + `llama3` → keeps `max_tokens` (don't over-match)
- `""` / `None` model → URL-only rule still applies (no regression)

### Impact

- **Severity**: P1 for anyone self-hosting an OpenAI-compatible gateway and pointing hermes at a new-family model. 100% failure rate on first turn — the agent is unusable until the user either switches to `api.openai.com` directly or renames the model to a legacy family.
- **Versions affected**: as far back as the `api.openai.com` hostname check was added; current `HEAD` (`ff975241`) still has the bug.

### Environment

- Hermes: `HEAD` (ff975241, 2026-04)
- Python: 3.13.5
- OS: `debian:13.4` container (official `Dockerfile`), host Windows 11 / WSL2
- Backend: self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway serving `gpt-5.4`

items.title: Context compressor summary fallback retry passes wrong arguments

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary
When `ContextCompressor._generate_summary()` falls back from an unavailable `summary_model` to the main model, the immediate retry call passes the wrong arguments.

In `agent/context_compressor.py`, the fallback branch currently does:

```python
return self._generate_summary(messages, summary_budget)
```

But `_generate_summary()` is defined as:

```python
def _generate_summary(self, turns_to_summarize, focus_topic=None)
```

## Impact
- `messages` is undefined in that scope, so the fallback path can raise `NameError` instead of retrying.
- The second positional argument is interpreted as `focus_topic`, so even if the first bug were fixed, the retry would still pass the wrong value.
- This only triggers when the configured `summary_model` is unavailable and compression tries to fall back to the main model.

## Expected behavior
The retry should reuse the original `turns_to_summarize` and preserve `focus_topic`, e.g.:

```python
return self._generate_summary(turns_to_summarize, focus_topic=focus_topic)
```

## Reproduction sketch
1. Configure a `summary_model` that returns a permanent error like 404 / model-not-found.
2. Trigger context compression.
3. Observe the fallback path fail instead of successfully retrying on the main model.

items.title: [Bug]: Multi-step deployment task context completely lost after API 400 error — agent asks user to repeat already-known info

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a multi-step deployment task encounters an API 400 error mid-execution, the agent completely loses all prior context about the task. On the next turn, instead of recovering from where it left off, the agent acts as if the conversation never happened — even asking the user basic questions it already knew the answer to.

## Reproduction Steps

1. User asks agent to deploy a service (e.g., "deploy lobehub v2")
2. Agent begins multi-step deployment: researching docs, pulling Docker images, writing config files, creating docker-compose.yml — takes 10-20+ minutes across many iterations
3. Agent encounters HTTP 400 error from the LLM provider (e.g., `Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 13`)
4. Error triggers fallback, which also fails with 400
5. User sends "continue" / asks agent to keep going
6. **Agent loses ALL prior context** — asks "which machine should I deploy to?" despite having already known the target server and being 80%+ done with the deployment

## Real-World Example

- Task: Deploy LobeHub v2 Docker stack on a specific VPS
- Agent had already: pulled all Docker images, created docker-compose.yml, .env, searxng-settings.yml, bucket.config.json, started containers
- Containers were running but with a config error (KEY_VAULTS_SECRET wrong length)
- API 400 error interrupted the session
- On next turn: agent asked "which VPS do you want to install on?" — completely forgetting it was already deployed on the target server

## Expected Behavior

After an API error interrupts the conversation, the agent should:
1. Check filesystem state (existing project directories, running containers, recent files)
2. Resume from where it left off, not restart from scratch
3. At minimum, NOT ask questions it already had the answer to in the same session

## Root Cause Analysis

The HTTP 400 error likely causes the context window to be truncated/reset, and the compressed context loses the critical task state. Unlike issue #11914 (MiniMax 529 fallback), this is about the error causing a **complete context wipe** rather than a degraded fallback.

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Checkpoint critical state to memory mid-task**: When executing multi-step deployments, the agent should proactively save progress (e.g., `memory add "Deploying X on server Y, phase: config_fix"`) so it can recover after context loss
2. **Auto-recovery on context loss**: Before asking the user clarifying questions, scan the filesystem for recent project directories, running containers, and recent file changes to infer what was in progress
3. **Error-resilient context preservation**: When a provider returns 400, preserve the current conversation context rather than resetting it — the error is in the API call, not in the accumulated context

## Environment

- Provider: custom (z-ai/glm5)
- Platform: Discord
- Task type: Multi-step Docker deployment (~15+ tool calls)
- Error: `HTTP 400: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 13 (char 12)` — BadRequestError

## Related Issues

- #7255 — Context compression drops in-progress tool_call chains
- #11914 — Context compression causes permanent task loss after MiniMax 529
- #13840 — session_search compression black hole
- #9413 — Context compression drops recent conversation and injects cross-session fragments

### Bug Description

    auxiliary_client.py の resolve_provider_client() が auth_type == "aws_sdk" (Bedrock) を
    未処理のまま return None, None にフォールスルーする。

    Symptom

    ログに以下が繰り返し出力される:
      resolve_provider_client: unhandled auth_type aws_sdk for bedrock

    その結果、以下の機能が完全に動作しなくなる:
    - Context compression (自動コンテキスト圧縮)
    - Memory flush (メモリ書き込み)
    - Summarization (ターン要約)

### Steps to Reproduce

    1. config.yaml で model.provider: bedrock を設定する
    2. 長い会話を行い、context compression が発火する状態を作る
    3. ログに unhandled auth_type aws_sdk for bedrock が繰り返し出現
    4. middle turns が要約なしで削除される

### Expected Behavior

Bedrockをメインプロバイダーに使っている場合、auxiliary機能もBedrockの認証をそのまま使えるべき。

### Actual Behavior

auxiliary_client.py の resolve_provider_client() が auth_type "aws_sdk" を処理できず、
  繰り返し以下の警告をログに出力し、auxiliary 機能が完全に無効になる：

    WARNING resolve_provider_client: unhandled auth_type aws_sdk for bedrock
    WARNING Auxiliary auto-detect: no provider available (tried: openrouter, nous,
    local/custom, openai-codex, api-key). Compression, summarization, and memory
    flush will not work.

  結果：
  - コンテキスト圧縮が動作せず、長い会話で middle turns が要約なしに削除される
  - メモリ flush が機能しない
  - セッション要約が生成されない

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
ファイル: agent/auxiliary_client.py, resolve_provider_client() 行1863付近

  原因:
    resolve_provider_client() は openrouter, nous, anthropic, custom,
    openai-codex, api_key 等の auth_type を処理するが、
    auth_type == "aws_sdk" (Bedrock) の分岐が存在しない。
    そのため最後の fallthrough に到達し return None, None となる。

  コードフロー:
    1. config.yaml で model.provider: bedrock を設定
    2. auxiliary auto-detect が main provider (bedrock) を使おうとする
    3. resolve_provider_client("bedrock", model) が呼ばれる
    4. PROVIDER_REGISTRY から bedrock の pconfig を取得 → auth_type = "aws_sdk"
    5. aws_sdk に対応する elif 分岐がないため行1863に到達
    6. "unhandled auth_type aws_sdk for bedrock" を警告して None を返す
    7. fallback chain (openrouter, nous 等) も全て認証情報なしで失敗
    8. auxiliary 機能が完全に無効化

  再現手順:
    1. config.yaml に model.provider: bedrock, model.default: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 を設定
    2. OPENROUTER_API_KEY 等の外部APIキーを設定しない
    3. hermes chat を起動
    4. tail -f ~/.hermes/logs/errors.log で警告を確認

  修正案:
    resolve_provider_client() に aws_sdk 分岐を追加し、
    Bedrock API (AnthropicBedrock SDK or Converse API) を
    OpenAI互換 .chat.completions.create() でラップするアダプターを返す。
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04

### Python Version

3.11.9

### Hermes Version

0.10.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

    agent/auxiliary_client.py 行 1863 付近:

      logger.warning("resolve_provider_client: unhandled auth_type %s for %s",
                     pconfig.auth_type, provider)
      return None, None  # ← aws_sdk ケースが未実装

    auth_type が api_key / oauth の分岐は実装済みだが、aws_sdk ブランチが存在しない。

### Proposed Fix (optional)

    resolve_provider_client() に aws_sdk 分岐を追加:

      if pconfig.auth_type == "aws_sdk":
          from anthropic import AnthropicBedrock
          bedrock_client = AnthropicBedrock()  # boto3 credential chain を使用
          return BedrockOpenAIAdapter(bedrock_client), model

    または boto3 + Bedrock Converse API を直接使い、OpenAI SDK の ChatCompletion
    レスポンス形式に変換するアダプタークラスを実装する。

    Impact

    - Bedrock をメインプロバイダーとして使う全ユーザーに影響
    - 長い会話で middle turns が要約なしで削除され、会話品質が低下する
    - warning ログのみでエラーにならないためサイレントな機能不全になる

    agent/auxiliary_client.py line ~1863

items.title: [Bug]: docker compose build fails with 'invalid file request' when container writes broken symlinks to bind-mounted /opt/data
items.body:
### Bug Description

When the published Docker deployment writes runtime state into the bind-mounted `./data` directory, the next `docker compose build` can abort with:

```
ERROR: failed to build: failed to solve: invalid file request data/.config/pulse/<host>-runtime
```

The direct trigger is a **dangling symlink** — PulseAudio creates `data/.config/pulse/<host>-runtime -> /tmp/pulse-<random>`, whose target only exists inside the container. Docker's tar packer walks the build context on the host, follows the broken symlink, and fails.

The root cause is broader than PulseAudio, though: the [`Dockerfile`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/Dockerfile#L53) declares `VOLUME /opt/data` and the compose recipe bind-mounts `./data:/opt/data` for runtime state, but [`.dockerignore`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/.dockerignore) does not list `data/`. Anything the container writes under `/opt/data` — dangling symlinks, unix sockets, character devices, large log files — leaks into the build context on the next build.

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
# Use the documented compose deployment with bind-mounted data/
cat > docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'
services:
  hermes:
    build: .
    image: hermes-agent:local
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true
    volumes:
      - ./data:/opt/data
EOF

docker compose build                       # first build succeeds (data/ empty)
docker compose run --rm hermes doctor      # container writes XDG runtime symlink into /opt/data
ls -la data/.config/pulse/                 # -> <host>-runtime -> /tmp/pulse-<random>  (dangling on host)
docker compose build                       # ERROR: invalid file request data/.config/pulse/<host>-runtime
```

### Expected Behavior

`.dockerignore` excludes `data/` so runtime state under the bind-mounted volume never enters the build context.

### Actual Behavior

Runtime data is walked as part of the build context. Any non-regular file (dangling symlink, socket, device) that the container happens to create there breaks every subsequent build, until the user manually cleans `data/`.

### Root Cause

[`.dockerignore`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/.dockerignore) excludes `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `.github`, `.env`, `*.md`, but **not** `data/`. The repository [`.gitignore`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/.gitignore) already lists `data/` (correctly treating it as runtime state), so the exclusion is simply missing from `.dockerignore`.

### Proposed Fix

One-line addition to `.dockerignore`:

```diff
 # Environment files
 .env

 *.md
+
+# Runtime data (bind-mounted at /opt/data; must not leak into build context)
+data/
```

Also shrinks the build context (logs, sessions, memories, skills, cron state under `data/` no longer shipped to the daemon on every build).

### Impact

- **Severity**: hard failure on rebuild for every compose user whose container has written any non-regular file to `/opt/data`. PulseAudio is the common trigger (voice mode, WSL bridge, any Playwright/Chromium invocation that pulls in audio libs), but the class of problem is general — unix sockets, character devices, and dangling symlinks all fail the same way.
- **Severity on success path**: even when the build succeeds, context size grows monotonically with runtime usage (logs, session history, cached memories all shipped to the daemon).
- **Versions affected**: current `HEAD` (`ff975241`) and every version since the Docker image was introduced in #3668.

### Relation to existing PRs

- #6092 (open) adds Python/IDE patterns but not `data/`.
- #4444 (open) is a full multi-stage Dockerfile refactor that *does* include `data/` as part of a broader `.dockerignore` rewrite; this one-line fix is the minimal interim for users who want rebuilds to keep working on current `main` without waiting for that refactor to land.
- #8904 (merged), #8838 (closed) address `.venv` only.

### Environment

- Hermes: `HEAD` (`ff975241`, 2026-04)
- Docker: 28.5.2, Compose v2.40.3
- Host: Windows 11 Enterprise / Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend
- Container base: `debian:13.4`

### Bug Description

2. Line 579: `os.kill(pid, 0)` (Global PID lock check)

### Expected Behavior
- `hermes gateway` starts successfully on native Windows
- PID existence check works without Windows compatibility errors

### Debug Report (hermes debug share)
> Note: `hermes debug share` fails to run on native Windows due to the same `os.kill(pid, 0)` error (gateway cannot start to generate debug links). Below is the core debug information collected manually:

>   asyncio==3.4.3
>   uv==0.1.31

# Line 343 in gateway/status.py (Feishu lock check)
            try:

## Bug Description

When a user has a **Moonshot AI Global API key** (from `platform.moonshot.ai`) and sets it up in Hermes, they see **"kimi-coding"** in the provider list and model picker. This naming is confusing because:

- **`kimi-coding`** provider → `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` (requires a Kimi Coding-specific key — a separate product)
- **`moonshotai`** provider → `api.moonshot.ai/v1` (for standard Moonshot API keys from platform.moonshot.ai)

Users with regular Moonshot Global API keys expect "kimi-coding" to work with their `platform.moonshot.ai` key — but it does not, because it points to a **different API endpoint** and different billing system.

**Error they see when trying to use `kimi-coding` with a standard Moonshot key:**
```
API call failed: HTTP 401: Invalid Authentication
```

## Expected Behavior

Users with Moonshot AI Global API keys (platform.moonshot.ai) should either:

1. Have the **`moonshotai`** provider appear in the model picker (it has all the Kimi models: kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, etc.) — not just `kimi-coding`
2. OR the `kimi-coding` provider label should clearly indicate it requires a **kimi.com/coding** key, not a platform.moonshot.ai key
3. OR during `hermes setup`, when selecting Kimi/Moonshot, ask which platform the user is registering on: `platform.moonshot.ai` vs `kimi.com/coding`

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.10.0
- Moonshot AI Global API key (from platform.moonshot.ai)
- KIMI_API_KEY env var set
- Provider shown as `kimi-coding` in `hermes model` picker

## Note for contributors

The `moonshotai` provider exists in `models_dev_cache.json` with all the correct Kimi models (kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, etc.) and correct endpoint (`api.moonshot.ai/v1`). It just does not get shown in the model picker because there is no auth entry seeded for it. Meanwhile `kimi-coding` gets shown but points to the wrong endpoint for standard Moonshot API keys.

items.body:
### Bug Description

The skill index injected into the system prompt hard-truncates every skill description to 60 characters. This means the vast majority of skills have their descriptions cut off with '...', potentially stripping the trigger criteria and context the model needs to route correctly.

Meanwhile, the skills_tool.py module defines MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 1024 and enforces that limit when the agent calls skills_list() at runtime. But the system prompt builder uses a completely separate code path with its own hardcoded 60-char limit.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a skill with a description longer than 60 characters
2. Start a Hermes session
3. Inspect the system prompt - the <available_skills> block shows truncated descriptions:

items.title: [Bug]: Allow users to opt into preserve_dots for third-party Bedrock-style proxies

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

When using a custom Anthropic-compatible endpoint that follows the AWS
Bedrock dotted-model-id convention (e.g. `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`),
Hermes rewrites the dot to a hyphen and the endpoint returns HTTP 404
`"The model 'anthropic-claude-X' does not exist"`. The rewrite is gated
by a hardcoded host allowlist in `_anthropic_preserve_dots()`; there is
no config-level opt-in.

I can get it working by adding my proxy's host substring to the
allowlist in source, but this doesn't scale — every new third-party
Bedrock-style proxy needs an upstream PR. A user-facing config knob
would solve this once.

### Steps to Reproduce


Config:

```yaml
model:
  default: anthropic.claude-opus-4-7
  provider: custom
  base_url: https://<bedrock-proxy>.example.com/anthropic
  api_mode: anthropic_messages           # also auto-detected from /anthropic suffix
```


### Expected Behavior

it should work with the base url provided by user

### Actual Behavior


The proxy exposes Anthropic models only via `/anthropic/v1/messages`
and expects the dotted Bedrock inference-profile form
(`anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`), rejecting the hyphenated form.

First request fails:

```
HTTP 404: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error",
"message":"The model 'anthropic-claude-opus-4-7' does not exist"}}
```

The request went out with `anthropic-claude-opus-4-7` (hyphen), not the
configured `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (dot).


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
NA
```

### Operating System

MacOS 26.4.1

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Root cause

`agent/run_agent.py` → `_anthropic_preserve_dots()` returns `True` only
for a closed set of hosts (`dashscope`, `aliyuncs`, `minimax`,
`opencode.ai/zen/`, `bigmodel.cn`, `bedrock-runtime.`). For any other
base URL — including third-party Bedrock proxies that serve the same
dotted ids — `normalize_model_name()` strips the dots. That's correct
for OpenRouter-style `claude-opus-4.6` but wrong for
Bedrock-style `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`.

## Workaround (local patch)

```python
# agent/run_agent.py, inside _anthropic_preserve_dots()
base = (getattr(self, "base_url", "") or "").lower()
return (
    "dashscope" in base
    or "aliyuncs" in base
    or "minimax" in base
    or "opencode.ai/zen/" in base
    or "bigmodel.cn" in base
    or "bedrock-runtime." in base
    or "<my-proxy-host>." in base          # ← local addition
)
```

Works, but has to be re-applied on every Hermes upgrade.



### Proposed Fix (optional)



Add a user-facing override so the allowlist doesn't have to grow with
every new proxy.

**Option A — explicit config flag (preferred).** Respect a
`model.preserve_dots` boolean if set:

```yaml
model:
  default: anthropic.claude-opus-4-7
  provider: custom
  base_url: https://<bedrock-proxy>.example.com/anthropic
  api_mode: anthropic_messages
  preserve_dots: true        # ← new: force-true, bypass host allowlist
```

Sketch:

```python
def _anthropic_preserve_dots(self) -> bool:
    # Explicit user override wins.
    override = getattr(self, "model_preserve_dots", None)
    if isinstance(override, bool):
        return override
    # ... existing provider/host allowlist unchanged ...
```

**Option B — extra host list.** Read additional substrings from
`model.preserve_dots_hosts: [...]` and fold them into the existing
check. Lower-magic but a little more to configure.

Either works. Option A is simpler and matches how
`api_mode` already lets users override auto-detection when they know
what their endpoint expects.

## Why this is worth doing

- The existing allowlist has grown through several PRs (#5211 opencode
  fix, #11976 Bedrock fix) — each new proxy means a new upstream PR.
- Third-party Bedrock-compatible gateways are proliferating
  (LiteLLM, Portkey, various enterprise egress proxies). Each one
  that picks the dotted id convention needs the same change.
- `api_mode` already has this escape hatch — `preserve_dots` is the
  logical twin.


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: auth remove re-seeds manually added OAuth credentials from singleton auth store

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary
`hermes auth remove` does not fully remove manually added OAuth credentials whose source is `manual:device_code` / `manual:hermes_pkce`. After removal, the next `load_pool()` call re-seeds a fresh singleton OAuth entry from the underlying auth store, so the credential appears to come back immediately.

## Affected files
- `hermes_cli/auth_commands.py:317-352`
- `agent/credential_pool.py:1132-1190`
- tests demonstrating the current failure:
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_commands.py:239-329`

## Why this is a bug
`auth_remove_command()` only clears the underlying singleton auth source when `removed.source` is exactly `device_code`, `hermes_pkce`, or `claude_code`.

However, `hermes auth add` writes manual OAuth entries with prefixed sources such as:
- `manual:device_code` (`hermes_cli/auth_commands.py:224,243`)
- `manual:hermes_pkce` (`hermes_cli/auth_commands.py:194`)

`load_pool()` later re-imports singleton OAuth credentials from the auth store using the unprefixed source names (`device_code`, `hermes_pkce`), so removing a manual entry does not actually prevent the credential from returning.

## Minimal reproduction / evidence
Focused tests currently fail on `main`:

```bash
source venv/bin/activate
pytest -q tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_commands.py -k 'auth_remove_accepts_label_target or auth_remove_prefers_exact_numeric_label_over_index' -q
```

Observed failures:
- `test_auth_remove_accepts_label_target` expects 1 remaining credential but gets 2 because a fresh `device_code` entry is re-seeded.
- `test_auth_remove_prefers_exact_numeric_label_over_index` expects `['first', 'third']` but gets an extra `device_code` entry.

## Expected behavior
Removing a manually added OAuth credential should also clear or suppress the corresponding singleton credential source, so the removed credential does not reappear on the next pool load.

## Actual behavior
The visible pool entry is removed, but the underlying auth store remains intact, and `load_pool()` silently re-seeds a new singleton OAuth credential.

## Suggested investigation direction
Normalize `manual:*` sources before the cleanup branch in `auth_remove_command()`, or otherwise treat `manual:device_code` / `manual:hermes_pkce` as aliases of the singleton source they originated from.

items.title: debug share full-log truncation drops a whole line at exact byte boundaries

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary
`hermes debug share`'s full-log reader can drop the entire first retained line when truncating by byte count. In an exact-boundary case it returns only the truncation banner and no log content.

## Affected files
- `hermes_cli/debug.py:154-179`

## Why this is a bug
When the file is larger than `max_bytes`, `_read_full_log()` seeks to `size - max_bytes` and *always* calls `readline()` to skip a partial line:

```python
f.seek(size - max_bytes)
f.readline()
content = f.read().decode(...)
```

That is only correct if the seek lands in the middle of a line. If it lands exactly on a line boundary, the next `readline()` discards a complete line that should have been included in the retained tail.

## Minimal reproduction
```bash
source venv/bin/activate
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.debug import _read_full_log
import tempfile, os

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    os.environ['HERMES_HOME'] = td
    logdir = Path(td) / 'logs'
    logdir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (logdir / 'agent.log').write_bytes(b'abc\ndef\n')
    print(repr(_read_full_log('agent', max_bytes=4)))
PY
```

Observed output on `main`:
```python
'[... truncated — showing last ~0KB ...]\n'
```

The retained tail should still include `def\n`.

## Expected behavior
If the truncation boundary lands exactly at the start of a line, that line should be preserved in the uploaded tail.

## Actual behavior
The first retained full line is unconditionally discarded.

## Suggested investigation direction
Only skip the first line when the seek position is *inside* a line (for example by checking whether the preceding byte is `\n`), instead of always calling `readline()`.

items.title: [Bug]: `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` false positive causes spurious truncation continuation with local API proxies

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

`_should_treat_stop_as_truncated()` incorrectly triggers truncation continuation for non-Ollama setups. When using a local API proxy (e.g., proxy on `localhost:8000`) with a GLM model via the `zai` provider, normal `finish_reason=stop` responses are misidentified as truncated, causing Hermes to automatically append a continuation message that asks the model to "continue where you left off" — even though the response was already complete.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a local API proxy running on `localhost:8000` that forwards requests to a remote GLM model endpoint
2. Configure Hermes with:
   - Model: `glm-5-turbo` (or any model name containing "glm")
   - Provider: `zai`
   - Base URL: `http://localhost:8000/v1`
3. Send a message that triggers tool calls (e.g., ask the agent to create/update something)
4. After the tool executes, the model returns a normal text response ending with an emoji or non-punctuation character
5. Observe that Hermes treats the response as truncated and sends a continuation message

### Expected Behavior

The response should be delivered to the user as-is. The truncation detection should only apply to actual Ollama backends, not arbitrary local proxies.


### Actual Behavior

Hermes sends the following system message back to the model, forcing a continuation:

> `[System: Your previous response was truncated by the output length limit. Continue exactly where you left off. Do not restart or repeat prior text. Finish the answer directly.]`

This happens because `_should_treat_stop_as_truncated()` returns `True` for the normal `stop` response.


### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
See below.
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 22

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.10.0 (2026.4.16)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The issue is in `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` (line ~2550 in `run_agent.py`):

```python
def _is_ollama_glm_backend(self) -> bool:
    model_lower = (self.model or "").lower()
    provider_lower = (self.provider or "").lower()
    if "glm" not in model_lower and provider_lower != "zai":
        return False
    if "ollama" in self._base_url_lower or ":11434" in self._base_url_lower:
        return True
    return bool(self.base_url and is_local_endpoint(self.base_url))  # ← this line
```
The final `is_local_endpoint()` fallback is too broad. It matches **any** local endpoint (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, RFC-1918 addresses), not just Ollama. This means:

- `localhost:8000` (proxy) ✅ matches (wrong)
- `127.0.0.1:4000` (litellm proxy) ✅ matches (wrong)
- `localhost:11434` (actual Ollama) ✅ matches (correct)

`is_local_endpoint()` was presumably added as a catch-all for "locally hosted models that might be Ollama", but local proxies that simply forward to remote APIs (like proxy → zai API) do **not** exhibit the Ollama stop-token misreport bug. They correctly relay the upstream `finish_reason` as-is.

The full trigger chain requires **all** of:
1. `finish_reason == "stop"` (normal completion)
2. `api_mode == "chat_completions"`
3. `_is_ollama_glm_backend()` returns `True` ← false positive here
4. Messages contain a `tool` role message (tool call was made this turn)
5. Response is pure text (no tool_calls)
6. Text length ≥ 20 and contains a space
7. `_has_natural_response_ending()` returns `False` (response doesn't end with `. ! ? : ) " ' ] } 。 ！ ？ ： ） 】 」 』 》` or triple backticks)

Condition 7 is also worth noting — the punctuation whitelist is quite narrow. Ending a response with an emoji (very common for CJK users) is considered "not naturally ended".




### Proposed Fix (optional)

Remove the `is_local_endpoint()` fallback. Only match explicit Ollama indicators:

```diff
-        return bool(self.base_url and is_local_endpoint(self.base_url))
+        return False
```

This restricts the GLM stop-misreport detection to only true Ollama backends (matched by `:11434` or `"ollama"` in the URL). Other local proxies that correctly forward `finish_reason` from the upstream API won't be affected.

If a broader catch-all is desired in the future, it should be opt-in (e.g., a config flag) rather than silently matching all local endpoints.

items.title: Hermes hindsight setup delays profile env creation until first runtime init

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug description
`hermes memory setup` configures Hindsight local-embedded mode, but it does not immediately materialize the standalone Hindsight profile env that `hindsight-embed` itself reads.

After setup, Hermes writes the LLM key into `~/.hermes/.env` as `HINDSIGHT_LLM_API_KEY` and stores provider config in `$HERMES_HOME/hindsight/config.json`, but `~/.hindsight/profiles/hermes.env` is only created later inside the Hindsight provider's runtime `initialize()` path.

That means a user can finish setup and immediately run `hindsight-embed -p hermes ...`, but it looks like they still need to manage a second copy of the key/config manually until they have had at least one real Hermes session.

## Actual behavior
- `hermes memory setup` completes successfully.
- `~/.hermes/.env` contains `HINDSIGHT_LLM_API_KEY=...`.
- `$HERMES_HOME/hindsight/config.json` contains the local-embedded provider settings.
- But `~/.hindsight/profiles/hermes.env` is not created until the Hermes Hindsight provider later runs `initialize()` during a real session.

## Expected behavior
If setup selects Hindsight `local_embedded`, Hermes should eagerly materialize the matching `~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env` during setup, not only during first runtime initialization.

That way:
- standalone `hindsight-embed` works immediately after setup,
- users do not think they need to maintain two copies of the key,
- the UX matches what setup already implied was finished.

## Why this happens
The current bridge logic that writes the Hindsight profile env lives in `plugins/memory/hindsight/__init__.py` inside `HindsightMemoryProvider.initialize()`, not in setup.

So the profile env eventually appears, but only after the first real Hermes runtime path touches Hindsight.

## Suggested fix
When `post_setup()` configures `local_embedded`:
1. save the regular Hermes-side config as it does now,
2. write/update `~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env` immediately using the saved config plus the just-entered secret,
3. keep the existing runtime reconciliation in `initialize()` as a later sync path.

## Environment
- OS: macOS
- Hermes setup path: `hermes memory setup`
- Hindsight mode: `local_embedded`

If useful, I have a small patch + tests for this.

items.title: [Feature]: Support multiple QQ Bot instances in a single Hermes daemon

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I want to connect **two different QQ Bot accounts** (different App ID / App Secret) to the same Hermes instance, so I can have **two independent sessions running in parallel** — e.g., one bot for long-running tasks and another for interactive conversation.

Currently, the QQ Bot adapter only supports a single instance because:
- Environment variables are singular (`QQ_APP_ID`, `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET`) — no way to configure a second bot
- `platforms.qq` in `config.yaml` is a single config block, not an array

This is a general limitation that likely applies to other messaging platform adapters as well (Telegram, Discord, etc.).

## Proposed Solution

Support **multiple named instances per platform** in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
platforms:
  qq:
    instances:
      - name: "bot-primary"
        app_id: "APP_ID_1"
        client_secret: "SECRET_1"
        home_channel: "OPENID_1"
      - name: "bot-secondary"
        app_id: "APP_ID_2"
        client_secret: "SECRET_2"
        home_channel: "OPENID_2"
```

Each instance would:
- Maintain its own WebSocket gateway connection
- Have its own independent sessions and home channel
- Be addressable by name for `send_message` targeting

Environment variables could follow a naming convention like `QQ_APP_ID_1` / `QQ_APP_ID_2`, or `QQ_APP_ID_PRIMARY`.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Running two separate Hermes instances** (different `HERMES_HOME`) — works but is operationally expensive: duplicate config, separate processes, no shared memory, double maintenance overhead.
2. **Single bot with session isolation** — already works per-channel, but does not solve the parallel-interaction use case (user sees one bot window, not two).

## Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

## Scope

Large (new module or significant refactor)

items.title: [--tui] gateway exits 0 mid-turn when memory.provider: byterover (SIGPIPE flood, then exit_group(0))

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

In `--tui` mode with `memory.provider: byterover` configured, the python gateway process exits cleanly (`exit_group(0)`) mid-turn on almost every prompt submission. The TUI surfaces this as `gateway exited` and the session is unusable.

Switching `memory.provider: ''` (built-in memory only) makes the crashes disappear completely. Same hardware, same prompts, same provider, same everything else.

## Environment

- hermes-agent: `0.10.0` @ `77e04a29` (`fix(error_classifier): don't classify generic 404 as model_not_found (#14013)`)
- OS: Arch Linux, kernel 6.19.10
- Python: 3.14.4
- Node: v25.2.1
- LLM provider: copilot
- `brv` CLI installed and working (manual `brv_query` / `brv_curate` from agent succeed)

## Reproduction

1. Configure memory with byterover plugin:
   ```yaml
   memory:
     memory_enabled: true
     provider: byterover
     provider_config:
       auto_extract: true
   ```
2. Launch `hermes --tui`.
3. Submit any prompt.
4. Within a turn or two, the TUI shows `gateway exited`. Often on the very first turn.

## What `agent.log` shows

- A `gateway exited` line, no exit code, no traceback.
- No OOM, no signal kill recorded.
- `tui-stderr.log` is empty — no python-level crash.

## What `strace` shows

`strace -f -e trace=signal,exit_group -p <gateway-pid>` while reproducing:

- A flood of `SIGPIPE` on the python child (it's trying to write to a pipe that's been closed on the other end).
- Then a clean `exit_group(0)` — the python gateway voluntarily shuts down as if it received an EOF/shutdown signal on stdin.

So: nothing kills the python process. The python process loses its parent-side pipes (stdout SIGPIPE, then stdin EOF) and exits 0 like it was told to.

## What I do *not* know (being honest)

I did not trace the exact code path inside the byterover memory provider that triggers this. I only have the trigger correlation:

- `memory.provider: byterover` → reliable mid-turn crashes.
- `memory.provider: ''` → zero crashes across many prompts in the same session shape.

So this could be:
- A bug in the byterover plugin's hook (slow response, wrong protocol message, child subprocess interfering with gateway pipes).
- A bug in `ui-tui/src/gatewayClient.ts` reacting badly to whatever byterover sends/takes/returns.
- An interaction (timing / payload size / async ordering) between the two.

The user-visible fact is: **byterover-as-memory-provider in TUI mode makes the python gateway lose its pipes to the Node parent and exit.**

## Workaround

```yaml
memory:
  provider: ''     # was: byterover
```

Built-in memory continues to work. `brv` CLI is unaffected — manual `brv_query` / `brv_curate` from the agent still succeed (they shell out directly, not through the memory provider plugin). `on_session_end` byterover-commit hooks also continue to work (they fire after the gateway is already done).

## Useful follow-ups

- Add a try/except around the byterover prefetch path in the gateway so a misbehaving memory plugin can't take the whole session down.
- Log the EOF / SIGPIPE event in the gateway (`exit_group(0) after SIGPIPE flood, last activity: <hook>`) so this kind of failure isn't silent next time.
- Decide whether `gatewayClient.ts` should ever close the python child's stdin during an active turn — if the answer is "no", whatever is doing it is the bug.

Happy to run more diagnostics (full strace with more syscall categories, instrumented byterover plugin, ui-tui debug logs) if useful — just point me at what would help most.

items.title: "overloaded" server errors classified as rate_limit, exhausting credential pool

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

When a provider (e.g., Z.AI) returns a "temporarily overloaded" error (HTTP 200 with code 1305), Hermes classifies it as `rate_limit` with `should_rotate_credential=True`. This causes the credential pool to mark the API key as "exhausted" after just 2 errors, making all further retries useless.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a provider that occasionally returns overloaded errors (e.g., Z.AI with a single API key)
2. Trigger multiple requests during peak load
3. Provider returns: `HTTP 200: The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later`
4. After 2 errors, the single API key is marked exhausted
5. All subsequent retries fail immediately with no valid credential

### Expected Behavior

"Overloaded" errors should be classified as server-side issues (`FailoverReason.overloaded`), NOT as rate limits. The credential is valid — the server is just busy. Rotating credentials is counterproductive and exhausts the pool unnecessarily.

### Suggested Fix

In `agent/error_classifier.py`, add an overloaded check **before** the rate_limit check in both `_classify_by_message` functions:

```python
# Overloaded patterns — server-side overload, NOT a credential/billing issue.
# Must come before rate_limit check to avoid rotating credentials unnecessarily.
if "overloaded" in error_msg or "temporarily overloaded" in error_msg:
    return result_fn(
        FailoverReason.overloaded,
        retryable=True,
    )

# Rate limit patterns
if any(p in error_msg for p in _RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS):
    ...
```

Also add overloaded patterns to `_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS`:
```python
    "servicequotaexceededexception",
    "overloaded",
    "temporarily overloaded",
]
```

### Related

Retry parameters (`max_retries`, `base_delay`, `max_delay`) are hardcoded in `run_agent.py`. Making them configurable via `config.yaml` would help users tune retry behavior for providers with volatile availability without editing source code (changes are lost on `hermes update`).

### Environment


- Provider: Z.AI (api.z.ai) GLM Coding Max Plan
- Error: `HTTP 200` with code 1305 "The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later"

items.title: Gateway service: exit code mismatch causes StartLimitBurst=5 exhaustion on rapid restart

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the gateway crashes or is killed unexpectedly, the systemd service enters a restart loop and exhausts `StartLimitBurst=5` within seconds, permanently failing even though the actual root cause may be transient.

## Root Cause Analysis

Two issues combine to cause this:

### 1. Exit code mismatch in `run_gateway()`

In `hermes_cli/gateway.py`, the `run_gateway()` function exits with code `1` on failure:

```python
success = asyncio.run(start_gateway(replace=replace, verbosity=verbosity))
if not success:
    sys.exit(1)  # ← Always exits with 1
```

But the systemd service file sets:

```
RestartForceExitStatus=75
```

This means exit code `1` is **counted** toward `StartLimitBurst=5`, while only exit code `75` would bypass the burst limit. When the gateway fails fast (e.g., "PID file race lost" which exits immediately without waiting), systemd cycles through all 5 restarts within seconds.

### 2. Zombie process edge case in `--replace` logic

In `gateway/run.py`, the `--replace` wait loop uses `os.kill(pid, 0)` to check if the old process is still alive:

```python
for _ in range(20):
    try:
        os.kill(existing_pid, 0)  # Signal 0 = existence check
        time.sleep(0.5)
    except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
        break
else:
    # Still alive after 10s — force kill
    terminate_pid(existing_pid, force=True)
```

`os.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for zombie processes (processes that have exited but not yet been `wait()`ed by their parent). A zombie process:
- Is still in the process table → `os.kill(zombie, 0)` succeeds
- Cannot respond to any signal → SIGTERM/SIGKILL have no effect
- Can only be reaped by its parent calling `wait()`

If the old gateway crashes and becomes a zombie, `--replace` will misjudge it as still alive, wait 10 seconds, then SIGKILL (which has no effect on zombie), and proceed — but the zombie PID is still in the kernel process table. Both the old and new instance then race to write the PID file, causing `FileExistsError` → "PID file race lost".

## Expected Behavior

1. Gateway should exit with code `75` (or whatever `GATEWAY_SERVICE_RESTART_EXIT_CODE` is) on startup failure, not `1`, so systemd's `RestartForceExitStatus=75` correctly bypasses the burst limit for transient failures.
2. The `--replace` zombie process check should use `os.wait4()` or check `/proc/{pid}/stat` to properly detect zombie state, not rely solely on `os.kill(pid, 0)`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: NousResearch/hermes-agent
- OS: Debian (WSL) / systemd user service
- Python: 3.x via venv

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start gateway normally: `hermes gateway start`
2. Kill gateway with SIGKILL (simulating crash): `kill -9 <gateway_pid>`
3. Observe: `systemctl --user status hermes-gateway.service` shows rapid restart attempts until burst limit is hit
4. Gateway service enters `failed` state permanently

## Suggested Fix

**Fix 1** — In `hermes_cli/gateway.py`, change `run_gateway()` to use the correct exit code:

```python
from gateway.restart import GATEWAY_SERVICE_RESTART_EXIT_CODE

success = asyncio.run(start_gateway(replace=replace, verbosity=verbosity))
if not success:
    sys.exit(GATEWAY_SERVICE_RESTART_EXIT_CODE)  # 75
```

**Fix 2** — In `gateway/run.py`, add zombie detection in the `--replace` wait loop:

```python
import os
import stat

def is_zombie(pid: int) -> bool:
    try:
        st = os.stat(f"/proc/{pid}")
        return stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)  # /proc/PID is a dir for alive processes
    except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
        return False
    # Alternative: check STATUS in /proc/{pid}/status for 'Z (zombie)'

# In the replace loop:
for _ in range(20):
    try:
        os.kill(existing_pid, 0)
        if is_zombie(existing_pid):
            break  # Zombie won't exit, stop waiting
        time.sleep(0.5)
    except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
        break
```

## Logs

```
Apr 22 23:10:48 XIAOXIN systemd[195]: hermes-gateway.service: Consumed 2.409s CPU time, 56.5M memory peak.
Apr 22 23:11:18 XIAOXIN systemd[195]: hermes-gateway.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 5.
Apr 22 23:11:18 XIAOXIN systemd[195]: hermes-gateway.service: Start request repeated too quickly.
Apr 22 23:11:18 XIAOXIN systemd[195]: hermes-gateway.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
```

---

*Filed via Hermes Agent*

labels.name: comp/cli

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# Bug: Duplicate provider entries in `/model` picker when providers exist in both built-in and user config

## Description
When a provider exists in both:
1. Built-in provider list (HERMES_OVERLAYS, CANONICAL_PROVIDERS, or _PROVIDER_MODELS)
2. User config (`providers:` section in config.yaml)

The `/model` picker shows duplicate entries with different names and model counts.

## Current Behavior
Example output from Hermes CLI TUI `/model` command:
```
Current: deepseek-chat on DeepSeek
› DeepSeek (2 models) ‹ current
OpenRouter (32 models)
Anthropic (8 models)
Z.AI (7 models)
Kimi For Coding (7 models)
OpenAI (0 models) 
openai (0 models)
 deepseek (0 models)
kimi-coding (0 models)
```

Note the duplicates:
- `DeepSeek` (built-in) and `deepseek` (user config)
- `Kimi For Coding` (canonical) and `kimi-coding` (user config)
- `OpenAI` (?) and `openai` (user config)

## Root Cause
The bug is in `hermes_cli/model_switch.py::list_authenticated_providers()`:

1. **Section 2** (HERMES_OVERLAYS) adds built-in providers (e.g., `slug="deepseek", name="DeepSeek"`)
2. **Section 3** (user-defined endpoints) tries to add user config providers but skips if slug already in `seen_slugs`
3. **Section 4** (custom providers) adds providers from `custom_providers` list with `custom:` prefix
   - Checks `if slug.lower() in seen_slugs:` where `slug="custom:deepseek"`
   - `seen_slugs` has `"deepseek"` but not `"custom:deepseek"`
   - Result: Adds duplicate `custom:deepseek`

The deduplication logic fails because:
- Section 4 only checks exact slug match, not base slug (without `custom:` prefix)
- `_pair_key` deduplication assumes Section 3 adds all user providers, but Section 3 skips providers already in `seen_slugs`

## Configuration
Relevant config.yaml sections:
```yaml
providers:
  openai:
    type: openai
    base_url: https://api.openai.com/v1
    api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY
    default_flex: True
    models: ['gpt-5.4', 'gpt-5.4-mini', 'gpt-5.4-nano']
  deepseek:
    type: deepseek
    base_url: https://api.deepseek.com
    api_key_env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
  kimi-coding:
    type: kimi-coding
    base_url: https://api.moonshot.ai/v1
    api_key_env: KIMI_API_KEY
```

## Expected Behavior
Each provider should appear only once in the `/model` picker:
- Built-in providers should show with their proper display names
- User config providers that duplicate built-in providers should be suppressed
- Providers should show correct model counts (not 0 for configured providers)

## Proposed Fix
In `list_authenticated_providers()`, Section 4 (lines 1161-1185):

Change from:
```python
if slug.lower() in seen_slugs:
    continue
```

To:
```python
# Check both the full slug and base slug (without "custom:" prefix)
base_slug = slug[7:] if slug.startswith("custom:") else slug
if base_slug.lower() in seen_slugs:
    continue
```

Additionally, consider improving the `_pair_key` logic to handle cases where Section 3 skips providers.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent version: (latest main branch)
- Python: 3.11+
- OS: Linux

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add a provider to `config.yaml` that already exists as a built-in provider (e.g., `deepseek`, `kimi-coding`)
2. Run Hermes CLI TUI
3. Type `/model`
4. Observe duplicate entries

## Additional Notes
- The "OpenAI" vs "openai" duplicate might have a different root cause (possibly from Section 1 or label formatting)
- Telegram `/model` picker works correctly because it uses different code path (`_build_model_keyboard` in telegram.py)
- This affects user experience by cluttering the model picker with confusing duplicates

Disclaimer: Issue written by Hermes Agent using DeepSeek ⚕️
